title: Could Homework Widen the Gap Between Families?
paragraphs: Many primary schools give children homework, and parents are often asked to help. But not every family can do this in the same way. A new study from the University of Manchester looks at this problem.

The researchers studied one mother, called Emma, and one teacher. Emma works until 8 in the evening, so she has little time for homework. The study says that some families have more time, more knowledge and more money than others.

The researchers think that schools may see a lack of time as a lack of interest. They also say that taking homework away may not solve the problem, because parents could be asked to help in other ways.

questions.q: Why does Emma have little time?
questions.a: She works until 8 in the evening.

questions.q: Will stopping homework solve the problem?
questions.a: Maybe not, because parents may be asked to help in other ways.
